page: Amazon Web Services i8g.48xlarge is a storage-optimized bare-metal-equivalent Nitro virtualized instance designed for data-intensive and high-throughput workloads. Powered by the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture, this arm64 system supplies 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at a clock frequency of 2.8 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning is substantial, featuring 1536.0 GB of RAM configured at an 8.0 GB per core ratio, backed by 36 MB of L3 cache per core cluster and 2 MB of L2 cache per core. Baseline networking capabilities reach 100 Gbps, and the hardware includes 45000 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD storage. The platform contains no hardware graphics acceleration.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate extreme aggregate processing capability alongside high data velocity. In stress-ng evaluations, the multi-core result achieves top-tier positioning at 314891.93, while single-thread throughput remains in the middle 50% band with a score of 1643.79, reflecting typical ARMv9 frequency profiles. Memory throughput is exceptional, recording 895.47 GB/sec uncached read and 411.91 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks. Database operations and low-latency cache tests yield superior metrics, highlighted by PassMark database scoring in the top decile and Redis SET execution reaching 349.81 million operations per second. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web delivery throughput similarly maintain top-tier performance tiers, while CPU-bound LLM prompt processing delivers average to weak throughput due to the lack of dedicated tensor accelerators.

The dense hardware configuration provides strong resource efficiency for infrastructure designs that require colocated ultra-fast storage and expansive memory. By coupling 45 TB of low-latency NVMe SSDs directly to 192 physical execution threads and 1.5 TB of memory, the system eliminates network storage latency bottlenecks. It is best suited for large distributed NoSQL databases, transactional relational engines, search clusters, real-time analytics pipelines, and high-concurrency caching tiers.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.48xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro system and powered by arm64 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, 1536.0 GB of system memory, 45000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and 100 Gbps baseline networking, without integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show exceptional multi-threaded computational and I/O capacity, evidenced by top-tier multi-core stress-ng results, 895.47 GB/sec large-block read memory bandwidth, and 349.81 million Redis SET operations per second, contrasted with moderate single-thread compute metrics. The vast local NVMe capacity paired with an 8.0 GB per core memory ratio offers high hardware density for IOPS-bound architectures. The server fits high-throughput distributed databases, in-memory caches, large-scale search indexes, and real-time data processing engines.
